matt: Observed tail-latency spikes in eu-west yesterday around 22:15. Correlated with a single tenant doing sustained large-batch jobs (~128k token windows). We saw routing churn + eviction storms. Proposal: introduce a 'burst-lane crediting' system — per-tenant token-bucket credits that allow short bursts beyond soft quotas, but trigger routing to dedicated/reserved pools or progressive throttling when credits deplete. Thoughts?

jia: +1 for credits. We need a clear metric for charging/backpressure and how this ties into existing QoS tags.

sam: We have soft quotas but no decay/credit model. Credits would need a recharge policy and an overflow behavior (route/reject). Also need to protect KV caches — short bursts shouldn't thrash caches belonging to other tenants.

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-331 — high tail latency eu-west. Link: https://incidents/redwood/331

raj: Cost question: if tenants can burst, how do we account for their bursts vs. reserved capacity? We should either bill bursts or deduct from a reserved credit pool. Maybe label pools: reserved (SLA) vs burst (best-effort).

carmen: Draft token-bucket example (conceptual):
```
burst_rate: 30 tokens/s
burst_capacity: 9000 tokens
recharge: 1 token/s per reserved_gpu_equivalent
overflow_action: route_to_burst_pool | degrade | reject
```
Map tokens to an approximate "effective token-seconds" derived from concurrency * seq_len.

matt: Exactly. Also propose automatic fallover: when tenant_credit < 20% and tenant has a dedicated pool, route there; if not, apply soft-degrade (reduce max concurrency and increase prefix-caching requirements).

jia: Can we add a short grace window post-burst where the system prioritizes warm KV cache rehydration for that tenant to avoid immediate miss storms?

sam: Implementation sketch: lightweight central credit ledger (redis) + local leaky-bucket fast checks on the proxy. Metrics to add: tenant_burst_credit, tenant_burst_consumption, burst_route_count, burst_reject_count. Instrument also kv_cache_evictions_during_burst.

deploy-bot: Staging job queued: burst-crediting-experiment-v1 -> canary -> eu-west/staging

matt: Plan: 2-week canary in staging, then a 5% traffic trial in eu-west. I'll write RFC + runbook and a dashboard for the metrics above. Anyone want to co-own the experiment?

raj: I can take cost/billing side: measure incremental GPU-hours and map to tenant billing adjustments.

carmen: I'll own KV-cache protection changes and the cache-warmth heuristic.

matt: Great — I'll open the RFC + experiment ticket and tag you both. Will include a rollback trigger: sustained +30% tail-latency for any other tenant for >10m -> auto-disable bursts. :thumbsup:
